name: FL-06
label: Safe R

key_factors: Fine's massive fundraising and outside-spending advantage
Prediction markets price Fine near 97% to win
No public polling of the race
model.rationale: The district's R+14 lean, incumbent Randy Fine's $4.3 million raised plus $3.7 million in outside support against Eric Yonce's $326K, and markets pricing Fine near 97% all point to a comfortable Republican win. With no polls or expert ratings to suggest otherwise, the fundamentals-based margin of roughly -16 stands.
model.watch: Any late polling showing Fine underperforming his partisan lean, or a surge in Democratic outside spending, would be the first sign of movement.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview: Randy Fine, the Republican incumbent, is heavily favored in this R+14 Florida district. He has raised $4.3 million and benefits from $3.7 million in outside support, dwarfing Democrat Eric Yonce's $326,000 in fundraising and leaving Yonce with limited cash. A Libertarian and an independent are also on the ballot but lack resources. Prediction markets give Fine roughly a 97% chance of winning, and no expert raters list the race as competitive. No public general-election polls are available, so the forecast rests on district fundamentals, the money gap, and market pricing. Fine's margin should be well into double digits, though first-term incumbents in special-advanced seats can occasionally underperform their lean.
